authoring_note: Mappings are interpretive and selective. They are intended to support triangulation with adjacent frameworks, not to claim one-to-one equivalence or shared licensing.

rules: Do not force one-to-one equivalence where the target framework operates at a different unit of analysis, purpose or level structure.
Preserve genuine gaps as non-mappings or contextual references.
Treat role-profile mappings as interpretive aids rather than formal accreditation claims.
Where a target framework is broader or non-digital, map the digital lens only to the relevant parts.

profile_mappings.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Individual Framework

target_frameworks.rationale: DigComp 3.0 is the closest public peer because it covers digital competence across work, learning and participation with clearly defined competence areas and progression logic.

what_transfers: Routine problem solving in digital environments
Choosing and configuring digital means to complete tasks
Awareness that effective digital use depends on more than access
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's explicit productivity and workflow lens is more operational than DigComp's area structure
DigComp distributes functional tool use across several areas rather than isolating it as a standalone productivity element

what_transfers: Creation and adaptation of digital content
Problem solving through digital design
Creative and purposeful use of digital tools
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc gives stronger weight to local workflow redesign and innovation in role context
DigComp includes programming and intellectual-property detail that is not central in all Jisc scenarios

what_transfers: Self-awareness about digital development needs
Deliberate growth in digital capability
Learning how to keep up with digital change
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc treats learning and development as a full element rather than as one competence within problem solving
Jisc places more emphasis on peer and organisational learning cultures

target_areas: Area 1: Information search, evaluation and management
what_transfers: Searching, evaluating and managing information
Judging source quality and relevance
Critical interpretation of digital information and data
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc combines information, data and media literacies under one element in a way that remains slightly broader in practice
DigComp's formal area names do not always foreground media literacy in the same way Jisc users may expect

what_transfers: Digital communication
Collaboration and participation in digital spaces
Awareness of digital interaction norms
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc more explicitly foregrounds participation in communities and collaborative work patterns in education settings
DigComp separates some identity-related competencies that Jisc partly connects here and partly in Digital Identity and Wellbeing

what_transfers: Managing digital identity
Digital safety and wellbeing
Balancing participation with risk and sustainability
what_does_not_transfer: DigComp gives more explicit treatment to cybersecurity, rights and sustainability themes
Jisc places stronger emphasis on relational wellbeing, boundaries and role-appropriate presence

genuine_gaps: DigComp 3.0 is more granular about AI, sustainability and rights.
The Jisc individual lens is more explicit about ongoing digital learning and about productivity as day-to-day workflow practice.

profile_mappings.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Teacher Higher Education Profile

target_frameworks.framework_name: UNESCO ICT Competency Framework for Teachers
target_frameworks.rationale: This is the closest public teacher-focused peer with three levels and competencies spanning teaching and learning, administration, professional development and policy alignment.

what_transfers: Reliable use of platforms and digital teaching workflows
Using digital tools to support core teaching administration
Operational capability in digitally mediated teaching practice
what_does_not_transfer: The Jisc profile is explicitly higher-education and practice-close
UNESCO CFT is framed for system capacity building rather than for a role-profile self-assessment bank

what_transfers: Design of digital learning activities and resources
Use of technology to support pedagogy
Purposeful innovation in teaching practice
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's creation element blends pedagogic design with local digital problem solving in a more granular role lens

what_transfers: Planned professional learning about digital teaching
Development of educators' capability over time
Using development activity to change classroom or course practice
what_does_not_transfer: UNESCO CFT is broader and more policy-facing than a teacher-facing feedback profile

what_transfers: Interpreting digital evidence for teaching decisions
Judging sources and data in pedagogic contexts
Using evidence to refine teaching practice
what_does_not_transfer: UNESCO CFT does not isolate information, data and media literacy as a standalone teacher element in the same way

what_transfers: Communication with learners in digital environments
Collaborative digital learning activities
Professional exchange and peer support
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's participation emphasis extends to fine-grained channel norms and community facilitation that are less explicit in UNESCO CFT

target_areas: Ethical and appropriate technology use as a cross-cutting concern
what_transfers: Responsible and appropriate digital conduct
Awareness of teacher presence, safety and trust
what_does_not_transfer: UNESCO CFT does not present digital identity and wellbeing as a discrete element
Jisc's explicit wellbeing and boundary-setting focus is more developed at the individual role level

genuine_gaps: UNESCO CFT is designed for policy, curriculum and capacity building across systems, not only for HE teacher self-assessment.
Level structures are both three-tiered, but the tiers are not directly interchangeable.

target_frameworks.rationale: The published Jisc HE teacher profile is officially mapped to PSF 2023, so PSF is an important adjacent reference for interpretation and local adoption.
genuine_gaps: PSF 2023 is a professional standards framework, not a digital capability role profile.
This deliverable does not claim fellowship or descriptor equivalence.

profile_mappings.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Researcher Profile

target_frameworks.rationale: The researcher profile is explicitly cross-referenced with the Vitae RDF, making it the most relevant peer framework for research role interpretation.

what_transfers: Using digital tools and methods to progress research reliably
Managing research workflow and project organisation
Operational fluency in research environments
what_does_not_transfer: RDF is not a digital-only framework and does not isolate productivity in the same way

what_transfers: Designing digital methods and outputs
Problem solving in the research process
Creating reusable research artefacts
what_does_not_transfer: RDF spreads creative digital practice across wider research competencies rather than treating it as a standalone digital element

what_transfers: Developing new methods and skills
Reflecting on practice and growth
Supporting others' research development
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's learning element is more explicit about digitally mediated self-development and peer learning

what_transfers: Critical use of literature, data and evidence
Provenance and quality judgment
Interpretation and synthesis for research claims
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc also includes media literacy implications that RDF may not foreground explicitly

what_transfers: Collaboration in research teams and communities
Co-authorship and knowledge sharing
Digital participation in scholarly networks
what_does_not_transfer: RDF communication descriptors are not limited to digital settings, while Jisc is explicitly digitally framed

what_transfers: Managing openness, recognition and trusted identity
Balancing visibility with responsible conduct
Wellbeing and sustainability in research participation
what_does_not_transfer: RDF does not package identity and wellbeing as a single digital element
Persistent identifiers and online presence are more central in the Jisc digital lens

genuine_gaps: RDF is broader than digital capability and spans the whole researcher role.
No direct level equivalence should be assumed between the two frameworks.

profile_mappings.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Professional Services Profile

target_frameworks.rationale: The professional services profile explicitly takes account of AUA values and the AUA CPD Framework, making AUA the most relevant adjacent professional reference.

what_transfers: Reliable use of systems and workflows in service practice
Personal effectiveness in digitally mediated operations
what_does_not_transfer: AUA is a behaviour-oriented CPD model, not a digital capability element structure

what_transfers: Designing better digital service processes
Using digital means for improvement and innovation
what_does_not_transfer: AUA does not isolate digital creation as a named professional services strand

what_transfers: Ongoing professional development
Learning through practice and supporting colleagues' development
what_does_not_transfer: AUA is broader than digital capability and includes many non-digital CPD dimensions

what_transfers: Using data and information to inform service decisions
Judging policy and operational evidence
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's explicit media literacy framing has no close AUA equivalent

what_transfers: Working effectively with colleagues and stakeholders
Communication and collaboration across services
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's digital channel and participation lens is more specific than AUA's behavioural framing

what_transfers: Trusted professional behaviour
Boundaries, confidentiality and sustainable working relationships
what_does_not_transfer: AUA does not foreground digital identity and wellbeing as a standalone category

genuine_gaps: AUA progression is framed around self, others and organisation rather than around digital capability elements.
No direct level match should be inferred.

profile_mappings.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Learning Technology Profile

target_frameworks.rationale: The learning technology profile was developed with ALT and is loosely mapped to CMALT, so CMALT is the closest professional recognition reference.

what_transfers: Using platforms and tools reliably in practice
Judging technical choices in relation to learning needs
what_does_not_transfer: CMALT is an accreditation scheme evidenced through portfolio, not an element-by-level capability grid

target_areas: Design and implementation of learning technology practice
what_transfers: Purposeful digital design
Problem solving and innovation in learning technology contexts
Reusable implementation patterns
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's boundary logic is more assessment-ready than CMALT's reflective-accreditation format

target_areas: Commitment to staying up to date
what_transfers: Ongoing professional learning
Reflective adaptation to change
Supporting others through knowledge exchange
what_does_not_transfer: CMALT is not organised as a three-level progression model

target_areas: Evaluation and evidence in learning technology practice
what_transfers: Use of data and evidence for technology decisions
Critical evaluation of sector and vendor information
what_does_not_transfer: Information, data and media literacies are more explicit in Jisc than in CMALT's overarching headings

target_areas: Communication and dissemination of effective practice
what_transfers: Consultation and collaboration with stakeholders
Dissemination and community contribution
what_does_not_transfer: CMALT is less explicit about channel choice and participation design

what_transfers: Professional digital identity
Sustainable and ethical practitioner presence
what_does_not_transfer: CMALT does not isolate wellbeing and boundary-setting as a standalone element

genuine_gaps: CMALT assesses reflective professional evidence rather than positioning people on a three-level role-profile grid.

target_frameworks.rationale: FELT adds an ethical lens around professionalism, values, care and community that is especially relevant to learning technology practice.

what_transfers: Reliable, responsible operational practice
what_does_not_transfer: FELT is ethical-principles based rather than operationally granular

what_transfers: Design choices grounded in learning need and values
what_does_not_transfer: FELT does not offer a direct creation/progression ladder

what_transfers: Critical awareness and ongoing professional learning
what_does_not_transfer: FELT is not a development-stage framework

what_transfers: Critical interpretation of evidence and claims
what_does_not_transfer: FELT does not separate data literacy in the same way

what_transfers: Inclusive participation, respectful collaboration and community-building
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc goes further on operational communication choices

what_transfers: Ethical presence, care, trust and sustainable practice
what_does_not_transfer: FELT is principle-led rather than levelled as identity management progression

genuine_gaps: FELT is an ethical framing device, not a directly equivalent capability framework.

profile_mappings.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Digital Leader Profile

target_frameworks.rationale: The closest reference point is organisational digital capability material, especially around culture, governance and leadership, but the unit of analysis is organisational rather than individual.

what_transfers: Using digital processes to support coordinated leadership work
what_does_not_transfer: No direct one-to-one element or level match exists

what_transfers: Designing roadmaps, experiments and change structures
what_does_not_transfer: Organisational models assess system maturity, not an individual leader's capability

what_transfers: Creating conditions for collective digital learning
what_does_not_transfer: The target resources do not define a personal learning progression in matching terms

what_transfers: Interpreting evidence, risk and benchmark information responsibly
what_does_not_transfer: Organisational and personal evidence practices are not equivalent

what_transfers: Building shared direction and participation around change
what_does_not_transfer: The organisational framework is not a communication-skills rubric

what_transfers: Leadership signalling around healthy digital norms
what_does_not_transfer: Organisational culture statements are not equivalent to individual identity-and-wellbeing stages

genuine_gaps: The closest adjacent references operate at organisational level, so strict equivalence would be misleading.

target_frameworks.framework_name: DfE digital leadership and governance standards
target_frameworks.rationale: These standards are useful as a sector-adjacent leadership reference, especially in college contexts, but they are institutional standards rather than a person-level capability profile.
genuine_gaps: The standards target organisational leadership and governance arrangements, not a six-element individual capability model.

profile_mappings.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Educational Developer Profile

target_frameworks.rationale: SEDA fellowship is the closest public professional-development reference for educational developers, especially around change, values, reflection and specialist outcomes.

what_transfers: Reliable facilitation and process management in digital enhancement work
what_does_not_transfer: SEDA is values and portfolio based rather than a digital productivity framework

target_areas: Specialist outcomes for design and change
what_transfers: Designing enhancement interventions and resources
Creating reusable approaches to curriculum or staff development
what_does_not_transfer: SEDA does not isolate digital creation as a separate strand

what_transfers: Reflective professional learning
Building learning opportunities for educators and teams
Supporting change through structured development
what_does_not_transfer: SEDA's level and fellowship routes are not equivalent to Developing, Capable and Proficient

what_transfers: Using pedagogic evidence and evaluation well
Interpreting data and scholarship for enhancement decisions
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's media and data literacy emphasis is more explicit

what_transfers: Facilitation, partnership and community-building
Inclusive collaboration across roles
what_does_not_transfer: SEDA is not specifically about digital channel choice or participation platforms

what_transfers: Trusted facilitative presence
Values, care and boundaries in development relationships
what_does_not_transfer: Digital identity and wellbeing are not packaged as a distinct SEDA category

genuine_gaps: SEDA fellowship supports professional recognition through values, outcomes and reflective evidence, not through a six-element digital capability progression.

target_frameworks.rationale: Educational developers often work alongside teacher-development agendas, so teacher-profile and PSF references can be useful adjacencies without implying equivalence.
genuine_gaps: Educational development work is facilitative and system-shaping, not simply a version of the teacher role.
